mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a contraction in economic activity, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent negative equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals a surge in economic activity, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent positive equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent negative equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which typically lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent positive equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which typically leads to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent positive equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) is growing and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, the combination signals an accommodative monetary policy supporting economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of GDPC1 growth and low FEDFUNDS does not correlate with subsequent positive equity returns.
